a: ‘As-sama’: what is meant is the sky, the celestial body.
‘Possessing the constellations’: a description of the sky; the buruj are the stations of the sun, the moon, and the stars in the sky.
‘Possessing the constellations’: a description of the sky; the buruj are the stations of the sun, the moon, and the stars in the sky.
‘The promised Day’: the Day of Resurrection; so called because Allah promised creation to gather them in it.
‘The promised Day’: the Day of Resurrection; so called because Allah promised creation to gather them in it.
One present, or a witness who testifies about others in it.
‘Mashhud’: no one will stay away from it because of the greatness of its matter.
Cursed and banished — an invocation of destruction.

‘The companions of the trench’: it is said they were a people of the Christians of Najran; the king of Yemen known as Dhu Nuwas called them to Judaism, they refused, so he dug a trench for them, kindled fire in it, and threw into it whomever of them he seized, one by one. In another narration, the companions of the trench are a group of the Jews of Najran who burned the Christians in Yemen to return them to Judaism.
A great, long cleft, like a moat.
The familiar fire of this world; fire is an active natural element represented by light and heat.
‘Possessing fuel’: a description indicating it is a great fire.
What fire is kindled with, or the blazing.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, past time.
The pronoun of the absent (third person plural).
‘Ala: a preposition conveying the meaning of literal superposition (being above).
‘Hum’: the pronoun of the absent (third person plural).
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative superposition.
It may be relative, described, or verbal-noun (masdariyya).
‘Al-mu’minin’: those who acknowledge the oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His messengers, and submit to Allah with obedience and to the Messenger with following.
Present, or witnesses: some of them will testify against others about that heinous deed on the Day of Resurrection, or they testify to that against themselves.
‘Naqamu minhum’: they seized them with torment, exemplary punishment, and severe penalty.
‘Min’: a preposition conveying the meaning of the beginning of the extent.
A particle of restriction; the exception here is called ‘emptied’ (mufarragh).
A verbal-noun particle conveying the future.

‘Allah’: a name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.
He is the Strong who is never overcome, for He, the Exalted, prevails over His affair; ‘al-‘Aziz’ is among the beautiful names of Allah.
He is the One worthy of praise, laudation, and commendation; ‘al-Hamid’ is among the beautiful names of Allah.
A relative noun for the masculine singular.
Lam: a preposition conveying the meaning of ownership.
‘His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth’: He is the Owner who disposes in the heavens and the earth.
The celestial bodies, and the upper world.
‘Al-ard’: the well-known planet on whose surface we live, or a part of it.

‘Allah’: a name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative superposition.
A word indicating comprehensiveness and totality; it is annexed either explicitly or implicitly.
A thing: what can rightly be spoken of, whether sensory or abstract.
A particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
A relative noun for a group of males.
‘They persecuted the believers’: they tried them and cast them into trial.
Those who acknowledge the oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His messengers, and submit to Allah with obedience and to the Messenger with following.
A conjunction conveying the meaning of delay between the conjoined.
A particle for negating the imperfect (present) verb and turning it to the past.
‘Lam yatubu’: they did not turn back from sins.
The fire with which punishment is given in the Hereafter.
Burning in the fire and perishing.
A particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
A relative noun for a group of males.
They acknowledged the oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His messengers, and submitted to Allah with obedience and to the Messenger with following.
‘Jannah’ in this world is a garden with trees, rivers, and fruits; ‘jannah’ in the Hereafter is the abode of lasting bliss after death.
‘Rivers flow’: their waters rush forth swiftly.
A preposition conveying the meaning of the beginning of the extent.
‘Tahta’: an adverb of place, the counterpart of ‘above’.
Plural of ‘nahr’: a wide elongated channel in the earth in which water flows, and also the flowing water.
A demonstrative for the distant masculine singular; one person is addressed with it.
Victory, success, attaining the utmost of what is sought, and salvation from everything disliked.
‘Al-kabir’: used to describe abundance of continuous quantity in concrete things, and sometimes borrowed for abstract meanings.
A particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
‘The seizure of your Lord’: His violent seizing.
Of your God who is worshipped.
‘Inna’: a particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
A pronoun referring back to the Word of Majesty (Allah), exalted is His status.
‘Originating creation’: creating for the first time without a prior model.
He recreates creation after its perishing, for the raising of the dead on the Day of Resurrection is by His power.
‘Huwa’: a pronoun referring back to the Word of Majesty (Allah), exalted is His status.
He is the One from whom forgiveness is abundant; ‘al-Ghafur’ is among the beautiful names of Allah.
He is the One who loves His righteous servants, is pleased with them, and accepts their deeds; ‘al-Wadud’ is among the beautiful names of Allah.
A reality that none knows but Allah.
He is vast in generosity, lofty in worth; ‘al-Majid’ is among the beautiful names of Allah.
‘Doer of what He wills’: nothing He wills is beyond Him.
‘Ma’: it may be relative or described.
A particle for asking about the content of a sentence; the question here is affirmative (taqrīrī).
Hadith: the speech that is narrated.
‘Al-junud’: the army, supporters, and helpers; what is meant is the disbelieving multitudes who denied their prophets.
The title of the kings of Egypt in ancient history; what is meant is the well-known Pharaoh of Musa.

An Arab people that perished before the appearance of Islam; named after one of the grandsons of Nuh, or so named because of the scarcity of water among them — it is said: ‘thamada al-ma’’, the water became scant; their prophet was Salih.
A particle of commencement, non-conjunctive, conveying the meaning of transition or emphasis.
A relative noun for a group of males.
They denied and did not believe.
A preposition conveying the meaning of state.

‘Allah’: a name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.
A preposition conveying clarification of the kind, or clarification of what is vague before ‘min’ or in its context.
An attribute of Allah, glorified and exalted; al-Muhit is the One who encompasses everything in knowledge, so nothing is absent from His knowledge.
A particle of commencement, non-conjunctive, conveying the meaning of transition or emphasis.
The Qur’an: the inimitable Book of Allah, which He sent down to His Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative containment.
‘A Preserved Tablet’: in it is recorded what was and what will be.
Guarded and protected; neither alteration nor distortion reaches it.
